concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 1 - Baseline Verifier Evaluation on Conflicting Instructions
concerns.text: User Story 1 has functional requirements (FR-001, FR-003) but lacks any Success Criteria. Add at least one SC (e.g., SC‑XXX) that measures the baseline verifier’s alignment score quality or runtime against the defined dataset.
FR-003 references '(See US-1)' but US-1 is undefined.
FR-004 references '(See US-3)' but US-3 is undefined.
FR-005 references '(See US-3)' but US-3 is undefined.
FR-006 references '(See US-3)' but US-3 is undefined.
FR-007 references '(See US-3)' but US-3 is undefined.
FR-008 references '(See US-2, US-3)' but neither US-2 nor US-3 are defined.

FR-001 says the dataset size must be "N samples (target N=1000)". The variable N is undefined, making the requirement ambiguous – it is unclear whether exactly 1000 samples are required or any size is acceptable as long as it is *targeted* at 1000. Clarify the exact cardinality requirement (e.g., "must contain exactly 1000 samples") to make the functional requirement verifiable.

FR-001 states that the dataset includes 'human‑annotated feasibility scores' that are generated via a deterministic antonym‑lookup/synthetic labeling procedure. Because the same lexical resources and rule‑based logic are also used by the symbolic constraint‑graph parser (FR-002), the validation target (human scores) is not independent of the predictor, creating a circular/tautological validation.

FR-003 requires the baseline verifier to be evaluated against the same synthetic feasibility scores described in FR-001. Since those scores are derived from the same rule‑based system that produces the graphs, the baseline alignment metric is not an external ground truth.

FR-005 specifies a paired t‑test/Wilcoxon test comparing baseline and graph‑augmented alignment scores relative to the synthetic human_score. Because the human_score is deterministically derived from the same rule‑based resources as the graph construction, the statistical test does not assess genuine improvement against an independent reality.

The assumption that a synthetic 'degree of partial compliance' metric can serve as a valid proxy for true human feasibility is questionable. Without collecting real human judgments (e.g., via crowd‑sourced rating of edit plausibility), the study cannot demonstrate that the graph‑augmented verifier aligns better with actual human perception.

new_concerns.text: FR-001 still requires synthetic feasibility scores for all 1000 prompts, but FR-003/FR-005 evaluate alignment only against human‑annotated scores collected for a subset (≥200). It is unclear whether the remaining 800 prompts are evaluated using the synthetic scores, which would re‑introduce a circular validation. Clarify that all alignment measurements are restricted to prompts with independent human annotations, or explicitly state how synthetic scores are used (e.g., only for auxiliary analysis).

responses.response: Added Success Criteria SC-009 and SC-010 linked to User Story 1 to measure baseline verifier alignment quality and runtime.
